definitions.explanation: a rough, informal way to refer to a person near the listener or previously mentioned; can be dismissive or contemptuous depending on context
an informal way to refer to an object near the listener or previously mentioned

examples.japanese: そいつとは{関|かか}わるな。
examples.english: Don't get involved with that guy.

examples.japanese: そいつは{面白|おもしろ}そうだ。
そいつの{言|い}うことは{信用|しんよう}できない。
examples.english: You can't trust what that guy says.

examples.japanese: そいつは{良|い}い{考|かんが}えだ。

notes:
CASUAL/ROUGH DEMONSTRATIVE:
そいつ is the rough/casual equivalent of それ (that) or その{人|ひと} (that person). It belongs to the こそあど demonstrative system.

こそあど DEMONSTRATIVES (ROUGH):
- こいつ - this guy/thing
- そいつ - that guy/thing (near listener)
- あいつ - that guy/thing (far from both)
- どいつ - which guy/thing

FORMALITY NOTE:
そいつ is very casual and can sound rude when referring to people. Avoid in polite conversation. Use それ/その{人|ひと}/その{方|かた} instead.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- そいつは{大変|たいへん}だ - That's tough/a problem
- そいつは{良|い}かった - That's great
